connector: What’s at the back of your closet? A wall, right? Today a girl named Lucy opens an old wardrobe, walks in, and keeps walking. Lewis builds a whole new world in one chapter. Look for the details that make it feel real.

a.raw: lucy looked back at the wardrobe and she could still see the empty room
a.fixed: Lucy looked back at the wardrobe, and she could still see the empty room.
a.why: Lucy is a name and starts the sentence. A comma goes before and, because and joins two complete thoughts. A period ends it.

b.raw: the faun had a red muffler and his skin was rather reddish too
b.fixed: The Faun had a red muffler, and his skin was rather reddish too.
b.why: The starts the sentence. Faun gets a capital because the Faun is used as his name. A comma goes before and. A period ends it.

mfill1.h1: Say tele, then phone. Now say them fast as one word.
mfill1.why: tele + phone = telephone: sound from far away.

mfill2.h1: Say tele, then vision. Push them together.
mfill2.why: tele + vision = television: seeing from far away.

mfill3.h1: Say tele, then scope. Type them as one word.
mfill3.why: tele + scope = telescope: a tool for looking far away.

mfill4.h1: Say tele, then gram. Push them together.
mfill4.why: tele + gram = telegram: a message written from far away.

cards.title: World Notes: Sent Away from London
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapters with your lens in mind.
text: The story begins during a real war, World War II.
In 1939, many children in Britain were sent away from big cities like London to stay in the country, where they were safer from air raids. An air raid is an attack by planes dropping bombs.
That is why Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy go to stay at the old Professor’s house.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. A new book starts today! Lucy opens a wardrobe and keeps on walking. Look for the details that make her new world feel real.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: a word part that means far, a new kind of sentence, and a lazy vowel sound.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 1 with your lens. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you brainstorm details about Narnia for your writing.

notes.wordParts: The word part tele means far. telephone = sound from far away. telescope = a tool for looking far away.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main idea and a part that cannot stand alone, joined by a word like when, because or although. When that part comes first, put a comma after it.
notes.spelling: The schwa is a lazy uh sound in a quiet beat of a long word. Any vowel can make it: the a in sofa, the e in seven, the o in lemon.
notes.wgrd: In a fantasy story, slow down and notice how the author builds the world: the weather, the light, and what could never happen at home.
vocab: eager to find out; very curious
a deep feeling of sadness or gloom
strange or unusual in a hard-to-explain way

mods.todo: Think about the question. Tap See what was hiding. Type each whole word.
mods.script: [curious] In Chapter 1, Lucy sees a light ahead of her. Not close by. A long way off. Far! There's a word part that means far. Tele. Here's a word that's not on your list. Telegraph. Long ago, a telegraph sent messages far away, over wires. Tele, far. Graph, write. Writing sent far! Read the four words and their parts. Then tap See what was hiding, and type each word.

mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Spiteful. Here's the sentence. Edmund could be spiteful, and on this occasion he was spiteful. He sneered and jeered at Lucy. One, read the sentence: he was mean to her on purpose. Two, look for word parts: spite, plus ful, full of. Three, check it. Spiteful means full of meanness. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

It can't stand alone! Add the main idea: she stooped down to feel it. When the part that can't stand alone comes first, put a comma after it. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then find where each comma goes.

Any vowel can make the schwa. Say the eight words in the sort, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Mr. Tumnus tells Lucy that he was going to hand her over to the White Witch.
items.why: He told the hard truth, even though it made him look bad.

items.t: Lucy tells Mr. Tumnus that what he did was pretty bad, but she says it gently.
items.why: Lucy wanted to be truthful and kind at the same time.

items.t: Mr. Tumnus pretended to be Lucy’s friend and asked her to tea.
items.why: Pretending is not honest. That is why he felt so bad.
